In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Coble hypersurface''' is one of the hypersurfaces associated to the [[Jacobian variety]] of a curve
of [[genus (topology)|genus]] 2 or 3 by [[Arthur Coble]].

There are two similar but different types of Coble hypersurfaces. 
*The [[Kummer variety]] of the Jacobian of a genus 3 curve  can be embedded in 7-dimensional [[projective space]] under the 2-theta map, and is  then the [[Singular point of an algebraic variety|singular locus]] of a  6-dimensional quartic hypersurface {{harv|Coble|1982}}, called a Coble hypersurface.
*Similarly the Jacobian of a genus 2 curve can be embedded in 8-dimensional projective space under the 3-theta map, and is  then the singular locus of a  7-dimensional cubic hypersurface {{harv|Coble|1917}}, also called a Coble hypersurface.
